text.p: Mexican media giant Grupo Televisa SA is widely expected to show better operating numbers in 1996, but extraordinary items will hurt the bottom line, analysts said.

Four analysts surveyed by Reuters said they expected an average loss of 2.15 pesos per CPO share, however, the company could show a gain of about 1.22 pesos per CPO, if extraordinary items are excluded, one analyst said.
That compared with a profit of 3.05 per CP0 last year, analysts said.
"It will be an accounting year for Televisa," Valores Finamex analyst Francisco Rivero said.
Televisa's operating fortunes are improving, though, after the sharp downturn in the economy hurt ad revenues.
Analysts expect 1996 revenues to come in at 11.43 billion pesos, compared to 11.299 billion pesos the year before.
Full year operating income is seen at an average of 1.016 billion pesos compared to 632 million pesos in 1995 due in part to lower costs.
The television and publishing group's earnings are seen posting a strong recovery in the fourth quarter.

Advertising revenues tied to "Top offs" or additional advertising payments, and those tied to the company's French plan -- a multi-media package offered to clients whereby advertisers prepay advertising for the following year -- are seen boosting revenues. Most deposits are made in October and November.
"You are going to have a very good fourth quarter because Televisa is a highly seasonal company, with most of the earnings tending to appear in the fourth quarter," one analyst said.
"The operating recovery will continue in this quarter, with increased sales that are higher than in the third quarter," Caspian Securities analyst Martin Lara said.
If the company posts a net loss, that will be tied to extraordinary items, some related to restructuring of the company, analysts said.
Televisa's earnings are considered difficult to foreast, partially because of differing expectations on foreign exchange or monetary gains or losses and by accounting changes.
